items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: Start off listening to Lester Young.

ctx.x: If you had the circumstances to teach a jazz class, let’s say a non-musician jazz class, let’s suppose they were like almost senior citizens, and some of the people said “I just don’t get it, when the musicians just start going off, I don’t understand what they’re doing.” Is there a way to explain jazz improvisation to that kind of person.

Yes. I would tell them they would have to listen more. You know they would have to listen more, and maybe start off not listening to Coltrane. Start off listening to Lester Young. It’s just like learning a language. If you had a little kid crawling here he’d be going ma-maw-mama — you know he couldn’t speak it, even though we are speaking. He would catch it and catch it and catch it and then by the time he is sixteen he would say “hey Monk, buy me a car.” He knows how to speak that. Or she knows. Right? So it’s…
listen to bla-bla-bla, you know? Sometimes you’ve got to acquire a taste or sometimes you don’t have time to acquire it, sometimes it hits you right away you just never knew it.
